# 🌍 Terraform Infrastructure as Code & State Mastery Track

Welcome to the **Terraform Infrastructure as Code & State Mastery Track** materialized by **Trak**.

This workspace is an in-depth curriculum covering HCL2 syntax, remote backends (S3 + DynamoDB state locking), `count` vs `for_each` edge cases, dynamic blocks, custom reusable modules, declarative `import` blocks, and native testing.

## 📚 Syllabus & Module Map

| Module | Title | Key Topics & Internals |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `00-setup-and-iac-architecture` | Declarative IaC & Core | Declarative model, Core vs Provider plugins, HCL2 parser, `terraform version` |
| `01-providers-and-versions` | Provider Configuration | `required_providers`, version pinning (`~> 5.0`), multi-region provider aliases |
| `02-resources-and-data-sources` | Resources & Lifecycle | `resource` vs `data`, `depends_on`, `create_before_destroy`, `ignore_changes` |
| `03-variables-outputs-and-locals` | Variables, Locals & Types | Input validations, sensitive variables, `locals` DRY patterns, outputs |
| `04-state-management-and-backends` | Remote State & Locking | `terraform.tfstate`, S3 backend, DynamoDB distributed locking, state migration |
| `05-state-manipulation-cli` | State CLI Operations | `state list`, `state show`, `state mv`, `state rm`, repairing corrupted state |
| `06-expressions-functions-and-loops` | HCL Expressions & Loops | `count` vs `for_each`, splat `[*]`, `for` loops, `can()`, `try()`, `cidrsubnet()` |
| `07-dynamic-blocks` | Dynamic Blocks | `dynamic "tag" { for_each = ... }`, nested conditional block generation |
| `08-reusable-modules` | Module Engineering | Standard structure, root vs child modules, publishing, version constraints |
| `09-workspaces-and-environments` | CLI Workspaces | `terraform workspace new`, workspace state isolation, multi-env patterns |
| `10-plan-apply-destroy-lifecycle` | Plan & Apply Lifecycle | `init -upgrade`, `validate`, `plan -out=tfplan`, `apply tfplan`, targeted destroy |
| `11-resource-import-and-state-recovery` | Declarative Import Blocks | TF 1.5+ `import { to = ... id = ... }`, generating HCL from live cloud |
| `12-provisioners-and-null-resources` | Provisioners & terraform_data | `null_resource`, `terraform_data` triggers_replace, `local-exec` caveats |
| `13-security-and-secret-management` | Security & Secrets | Sensitive attributes, Vault integration, KMS state encryption at rest |
| `14-policy-as-code-sentinel-and-opa` | Policy-as-Code & Scanning | OPA Rego policies, tfsec, Checkov, Trivy static IaC vulnerability checks |
| `15-testing-and-validation` | Native Terraform Tests | Terraform 1.6+ `.tftest.hcl`, mock providers, unit testing assertions |
| `16-ci-cd-automation-atlantis-and-actions` | CI/CD & Atlantis | Atlantis pull-request plans, GitHub Actions automation, plan approvals |
| `17-drift-detection-and-remediation` | Drift Detection | Out-of-band drift discovery, scheduled reconciliation in Terraform Cloud |
| `18-interview-questions-and-drills` | Interview Mastery Drills | Top 10 Terraform SRE gotchas + Production Reusable Module Design Drill |

---

## 🛠️ How to Practice
Each module contains:
- `README.md` — Deep theoretical explanation and architecture notes.
- `main.tf` — Fully runnable concept demonstration.
- `exercise/starter.tf` — Hands-on problem with `TODO` markers.
- `exercise/solution.tf` — Complete reference solution.

Setup And Iac Architecture is a core foundational concept in Terraform Infrastructure as Code & State Mastery that governs how resources, execution flow, and system state are managed.

## 💡 Why does it exist & Why use it?

- With `count`, removing an item from the middle of a list re-indexes all subsequent items, triggering unintended destroys and recreations.
- With `for_each`, each resource is keyed by unique map/set key (`aws_instance.server["node-1"]`).

## 🎯 Generating Nested Blocks Dynamically
```hcl
resource "aws_security_group" "web" {
  name = "web-sg"
  dynamic "ingress" {
    for_each = var.service_ports
    content {
      from_port   = ingress.value
      to_port     = ingress.value
      protocol    = "tcp"
      cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
    }
  }
}
```
